column1: # p348 — ACTION ZZ-x executed, both halves, and the denominator is the finding.
# p347 ran the HEAD-equality test and declared it done "over EVERY address on these shelves":
# 257 distinct addresses extracted from THE FIVE LIVE SHELF FILES.  Re-harvested here over ALL
#   p347's declared set (5 live shelf files, as its own header states)      440 casings
#   addresses appearing ONLY on the two APPEND-ONLY shelves               2 091 casings
# So the shelf-wide run covered 440 of 2 531 = 17.4 %, and its verdict column reads "unique HEAD
# across the shelf set" — a true statement about the set it measured and a false one about the
# shelves.  `agents/trending.md` and `repos/trending.md` hold 74 076 of this base's 122 217 shelf
# lines; they were excluded because they are append-only HISTORY, and the addresses on them are
# THE SPECIMEN, and folding cannot see it:
# ONE repository, published twice, under owners sharing no characters: the MIT Digital Credentials
# Consortium moved the project to the OpenWallet Foundation.  A case fold is blind to it; only
# HEAD equality sees it.  This is a FOURTH on-shelf alias pair, after p347's three.
# THE OFFLINE HALF, measured rather than assumed: 65 folded-collision groups on the complete set
# (the OWNER/REPO command template dropped).  Every member resolved first-hand with
# `git ls-remote --symref`.  64 groups answered and ALL 64 ARE SAME-HEAD — one repository under two
# or three casings.  ZERO groups came back with different HEADs, so folding produced no false
# positive anywhere on this corpus, which is the warrant for wiring it as `gate-fold-identity`.
# One group does not answer under either casing: gegok12/gegok12 / GegoK12/gegok12.
# Two of the 65 were already reported by p347 (OpenOLAT, RohanMuppa); the other 63 are new, and 63
# of them were invisible to `gate-identity` because it compares slugs case-sensitively.

column4: no false positive from folding anywhere on this corpus
